audience: Returning strategy players from the 2000s browser era
core_mechanic: A browser strategy game (islands, alliances, raids) whose first session is a staged gather-build-wait loop with an explicit first achievement set.
monetization: none during the measured period; under 20 dollars a month to run
title: Onboarding rebuilt five times because day-one retention was 25 percent
why_hot: A 2026 devlog with the honest number attached: day-one retention around 25 percent, five rebuilds of the first session, and the conclusion that onboarding is not teaching controls but getting the player to a first goal and to other players. Alliance members retained at 87 percent against 16 percent solo in the same game's later writeup.

core_mechanic: Arcade space shooter where consecutive hits raise a damage multiplier in visible tiers and any miss resets it to zero, with escalating screen effects per tier.
title: Visible combo multiplier as the whole retention spine
why_hot: A 2026 devlog that puts a number on the feedback loop: players who reach a 10x combo in their first run return the next day 70 percent of the time, against 30 percent for players who stay under 5x. The combo is always on screen, escalates in tiers at 5, 10, and 20 hits, and resets on a miss.

audience: Casual players arriving from a shared link on whatever device is at hand
core_mechanic: Not a game mechanic: a distribution thesis that the first playable frame is the product metric, with plain Canvas 2D as a deliberate size choice.
monetization: portal ad revenue on a 13-game catalog
title: Instant-play pages competing on first frame, not on features
why_hot: October 2026 measured numbers: median first frame 0.69 seconds on a first visit and 0.2 seconds on a return, about one kilobyte downloaded, against a GameAnalytics median mobile session of 5 to 6 minutes. The article argues the cost of starting is the differentiator now that WebGPU is in all four major browsers.
